memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "After Rachel gave birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, 'Send me on my way so I can go back to my own homeland. Give me my wives and children, for whom I have served you, and I will be on my way. You know how much work I've done for you.'" - Gen 30:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
With Joseph now born, something stirs in Jacob: a longing to go home. "Send me on my way so I can go back to my own homeland." After many years in Laban's household — years of hard work, deception, and family strife — Jacob's heart turns toward the land God had promised him, the place where God had met him at Bethel.

This homeward longing is a picture of something God plants in every believer's heart. However long we live in this world, with all its work and weariness, there is a deep sense that we are not fully home yet. We are, the Bible says, "foreigners and strangers on earth" (Heb 11:13), looking for a better country.

Jacob remembered God's promise to bring him back (Gen 28:15), and that promise drew him homeward. In the same way, God has promised His people an eternal home with Him, and that hope should draw our hearts forward through all the labour of this life.

It is good and healthy to feel that this world is not our final resting place. That restlessness is not something to suppress; it is a homing instinct God has placed in us. Let your longing for a better country keep you walking faithfully toward the home God has prepared (John 14:2-3).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I sense that this world is not my final home?
2. How does the hope of my eternal home shape how I live now?
3. What "homeward" promise of God am I holding on to?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You have prepared a home for Your people. Keep my heart set on that hope, and help me to walk faithfully toward the home You have promised. Amen.
